title: Biomimetic 4D Printing via Poisson Contraction Theory: From Layer-by-Layer Deposition to Boundary-Programmed Poroelastic Self-Assembly
content: Additive manufacturing and 4D printing enable complex soft structures, but the fabrication of continuous anisotropic membranes, embedded functional paths, and independently gliding interfaces remains challenging. This perspective explores a complementary strategy inspired by Poisson Contraction Theory (PCT): a mechanobiological hypothesis in which boundary-constrained tensile deformation promotes transverse contraction and fiber reorientation in fibrous, fluid-saturated materials. In a suitable poroelastic medium, the resulting deformation may couple to interstitial-fluid drainage and time-dependent consolidation; permanent planarization additionally requires a material-dependent stabilization mechanism. We translate these principles into three testable manufacturing concepts: (1) boundary-programmed membrane consolidation, (2) mechanically guided redistribution of embedded compliant or stiff inclusions, and (3) shear-conditioned formation of internal gliding interfaces. The third concept is explicitly speculative; localized mechanical stimulation has not been shown here to suppress cross-linking or produce an avascular surgical-type plane. We propose a staged benchtop proof of concept with measurable outcomes and controls instead of prescribing unvalidated acoustic parameters. PCT is presented as a design hypothesis rather than an experimentally established manufacturing method. Its value will depend on whether boundary conditions, transverse strain, fluid efflux, structure persistence, and interfacial friction can be independently quantified and causally linked.
